briefdescription.para: Appends the shortest decimal representation of a numeric value to a buffer.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The numeric type to format.
buffer
The string to append to.
v
The value to format.
Returns
Nothing.
The value is formatted into a local buffer, which is then appended to buffer.

For long double, a platform-specific path is chosen:
On Windows and on platforms where long double has the same storage width as double (e.g. 32-bit Arm), the value is cast to double and formatted with std::to_chars.
On all other platforms (e.g. x86-64 Linux/macOS with 80-bit extended precision, or AArch64 and RISC-V with 128-bit quad precision), snprintf with %.*Lg is used as a portable fallback, because std::to_chars for long double may be unavailable (e.g. when linking with lld). The precision starts at LDBL_DIG and is increased until the text reads back, with strtold, as the same value, up to LDBL_DECIMAL_DIG, which always reads back exactly. This gives the shortest exact form, as std::to_chars gives for the other types; a shorter form would need fewer than LDBL_DIG digits, and Lg removes the trailing zeros, so starting at LDBL_DIG does not lose it. For zero and the subnormal values, which have fewer significant digits, the precision starts at 1. The value of errno, which strtold may set for subnormal values, is preserved. If no precision reads back exactly, the C library handles long double with the precision of double (e.g. newlib on AArch64 and RISC-V), and the value is cast to double and formatted with std::to_chars, as above.

For all other numeric types, std::to_chars is called directly, providing locale-independent formatting. The snprintf() path uses the decimal point of the C locale, which is . unless the application changes it with setlocale().

briefdescription.para: Appends the hexadecimal address of a pointer to a buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Shared by the reporter and the expression_formatter, so that the pointers are displayed identically in the messages and in the expressions. Pointers to const or volatile objects, and function pointers, are accepted too.

T
The type pointed to (an object or a function type).
buffer
The string to append to.
v
The pointer.
Returns
Nothing.
Null pointers are rendered as "0x0", regardless of the platform, avoiding platform-specific representations such as "(nil)" on Linux/glibc. Non-null pointers are formatted with snprintf(), using the p specifier.

The p specifier expects a void*. Object pointers are converted implicitly to const volatile void*, which accepts any qualification, and the qualifiers are then removed with const_cast; a reinterpret_cast to void* would not compile for pointers to const objects. The object is not accessed. Function pointers, which do not convert to void* implicitly, use reinterpret_cast.

briefdescription.para: Prepares an operand of a comparator.

detaileddescription.para: The char arrays and the char pointers (not those of signed char or unsigned char, which are byte buffers) are converted to c_string, so that they are compared by content; the other arrays are converted to pointers to their first element, the functions to function pointers, and all other operands are returned unchanged, so the other pointers, arrays, and functions are compared by address.
The other operands are forwarded, so that the comparator moves a temporary, and refers to a named operand.

T
The type deduced for the forwarding reference.
t
The operand.
A c_string for the C strings, otherwise t, forwarded.
Arrays of char are converted using their size as a bound, pointers to char using the null terminator; the cv-qualifiers of the characters are ignored. Every other operand is forwarded, unchanged, as an lvalue or an rvalue reference.

briefdescription.para: Tells whether two numbers differ by less than a tolerance.

detaileddescription.para: If the three values are integers, the distance is computed exactly, as an unsigned value, also for operands of mixed signedness, and compared with the tolerance with std::cmp_less(), so that neither overflows nor wraps around. Otherwise, the values are converted to their common floating-point type, and the absolute value of the difference is compared with the tolerance. A negative tolerance, or a NaN, makes the result false.

Lhs_T
The arithmetic type of the first value.
Rhs_T
The arithmetic type of the second value.
Epsilon_T
The arithmetic type of the tolerance.
lhs
The first value.
rhs
The second value.
epsilon
The tolerance.
true
The distance between the values is less than the tolerance.
false
Otherwise.
For the integers, the larger value is selected with std::cmp_less(), and the distance is computed in std::uintmax_t: when both values have the same sign, as the modular difference of their conversions, which is exact; otherwise, as the sum of the larger value and of the magnitude of the negative one, saturated at the maximum of the type, which is then larger than any tolerance, as the true distance is. The tolerance is compared with std::cmp_less(), so a negative one gives false.

For the other types, the values are converted to their common type, which is a floating-point one, so std::int64_t values compared with a float tolerance lose precision; the comparison is strict, as in the tolerances of the floating-point wrappers.

lhs
The left operand.
rhs
The right operand.
The lexicographic order of the characters; a null pointer is equal to another null pointer and less than any string.
A null pointer orders before any string.

briefdescription.para: Orders a C string operand and a string.

detaileddescription.para:
lhs
The C string operand.
rhs
The string.
The lexicographic order of the characters; a null pointer is less than any string.
A null pointer orders before any string.

briefdescription.para: Compares two C string operands for equality.

detaileddescription.para:
lhs
The left operand.
rhs
The right operand.
true
Both are null, or both are strings with the same characters.
false
Otherwise.
Two null pointers are equal; a null pointer is not equal to any string, not even an empty one.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a C string operand is a null pointer.

detaileddescription.para:
lhs

briefdescription.para: Compares a C string operand with a string.

detaileddescription.para: Also used for std::string operands, which convert to std::string_view, and, as a rewritten candidate, with the operands in the reverse order.

lhs
The C string operand.
rhs
The string.

false
Otherwise.
A null pointer is not equal to any string.

briefdescription.para: Returns the value wrapped by a framework type, or the operand itself.

detaileddescription.para: If the type T is a framework type (see extension::is_op) that provides a get() member function, it is invoked and its result returned. Otherwise a reference to the argument itself is returned, so that the types of the application, even those with a get() member function, are compared with their own operators, without a copy. The selection is performed at compile time via if constexpr with an inline requires expression; the return type is deduced with decltype (auto) from the selected branch.
Always call it qualified, as detail::unwrap(), so that argument-dependent lookup cannot select a function of the application, defined in the namespace of an operand.
The operand is returned by reference, without a copy; the result is valid only as long as the operand.

simplesect.para: The value returned by t.get() for the framework wrappers (the literals and the to_* wrappers), otherwise a reference to t.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether two operands are equal within the tolerance of the floating-point wrappers.

detaileddescription.para: Used by compare_op for all six tags, so that a value within the tolerance is equal, and neither less nor greater; at least one operand must have an epsilon member (a floating-point literal, a to_f, to_d, or to_ld wrapper, or approx()).

Lhs_T
The type of the left-hand operand.
Rhs_T
The type of the right-hand operand.
lhs
The left-hand operand.
rhs
The right-hand operand.
true
The absolute difference is less than the tolerance (the smaller one, if both operands have one).
false
Otherwise.
The tolerance is the smaller epsilon of the two operands, if both have one, otherwise the epsilon of the operand that has one. The operands are equal when the absolute value of their difference is less than the tolerance.

briefdescription.para: C++ header file with inline implementations for the µTest++ internal detail namespace.

detaileddescription.para: This header provides the out-of-line template and inline implementations for all types declared in detail.h. It defines the bodies of the unwrap() helper, the unary and binary operator base class templates, the comparison tags, all relational, approximate, and logical comparator constructors, the predicate constructor, the tolerance helpers (within_tolerance(), differ_by_less_than()), the callable operator types (throws_op, nothrow_op), the append_number() and append_pointer() formatting helpers, the c_string operand and its operators, and as_operand().
Separating the implementations from the declarations keeps detail.h concise and focused on the interface, whilst grouping the complex lambda-based constructor bodies here for maintainability.
All definitions reside within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus::detail namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.
This file is intended solely for internal use within the framework and should not be included directly by user code.
